note: Measured on 2026-09-12 against /mnt/archive/datasets/melee/skirmish-gameplay/v2/fox-bf (the fox-bf pairing; not yet in a published SKIRMISH_GAMEPLAY_DATA snapshot, so this was run directly against the live pack, matching this loop's own instructions). Fixed since the prior baseline (-28, action_age): GuardOn/Guard/GuardReflect all enter with Ft_MF_SkipAnim (ftCo_Guard.c:386,509,790,901,1012), which skips the generic per-frame animation advance that otherwise brings cur_anim_frame back to 0 by the end of every other action's own entry frame -- state_age stays a constant -1 for the whole state (crates/skirmish-replay/src/observation.rs's action_age), not just its entry frame. Confirmed directly against this recording: P1 holds GuardOn then Guard for 21 frames (1430-1450) with state_age = -1.0 throughout, then GuardSetOff (Ft_MF_None, no SkipAnim) at 1451 already reports the ordinary 0.0; P4's own one-frame shield-drop at frame -28 (the fixed divergence) reports the same -1.0. 96 frames now match (-123 through -28); the new first divergence is frame -27, field position.y on P4 (expected 26.4701, actual 23.8001), on the same frame P4's GuardOn converts into Pass (falling through the platform). Diagnosed, not fixed: game::simulation::move_fighter's fast-fall trigger approximates decomp's real ftCommon_CheckFallFast (fighter.locomotion.tilt_y_age < an unexported ftCommonData+0x8C window constant, adjacent to the already-exported fast_fall_threshold at +0x88) with a previous_input heuristic; the platform pass already resets tilt_y_age to the 254 sentinel (matching decomp's own x671_timer_lstick_tilt_y = 0xFE reset in begin_pass) specifically to block an immediate re-trigger, but the heuristic doesn't consult tilt_y_age at all and fires anyway on this continuously-held down-stick, producing an extra frame of fast_fall_velocity instead of the recording's own pass_velocity + gravity. Blocked on the missing pack field (docs/parity.md); guessing the window value risks changing fast-fall timing elsewhere in the corpus, so this is reported rather than fixed with an unverified constant.
